Reason: The comparison between the normal prior radiograph (Fig. 1b) and the current admission film (Fig. 1a) demonstrates a new, well-defined elongated opacity along the right cardiac border that has developed within two years. This rapid appearance of a discrete mass in the anterior mediastinum is most consistent with a rapidly growing neoplasm, such as a thymoma or lymphoma, rather than chronic conditions or diffuse processes like pneumonia or effusion.
